stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
Represents a snapshot of current popular models within the large language model (LLM) ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google is integrating 'Personal Intelligence' into Gemini AI for in-car use via Android Auto and built-in Google systems.
The AI will access user data across multiple Google services (Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, etc.) to provide personalized assistance.
A key feature highlighted is the ability to query real-time information, such as flight status, while driving.

stories.title: SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: SpaceX plans its first attempt to fully recover the Starship orbital launch system and its booster next month.
Successful recovery would be a historic first for an orbital launch vehicle.
The effort aims to achieve full recovery of the entire Starship system.

stories.title: Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Gemini's personal intelligence capabilities are being integrated into automotive systems.
This signals a major shift in how advanced AI will be deployed in consumer hardware, specifically vehicles.
The article advises users to review their Gemini settings in light of this new integration.

stories.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch back end for TPUs
stories.author: ilreb
bullet_points: Google has open-sourced TorchTPU, providing a native PyTorch backend specifically for Google's TPUs.
This move significantly lowers the barrier to entry for researchers and developers wanting to leverage TPU hardware with the widely adopted PyTorch framework.
It represents a major step in democratizing access to high-performance AI/ML infrastructure by integrating proprietary hardware capabilities into open-source tooling.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when tested against the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla and SpaceX are reportedly discussing a potential merger.
Elon Musk confirmed the discussions during SpaceX's Q3 earnings call.
The merger talks are being conducted by special committees composed of independent directors at the request of shareholders.

stories.title: SpaceX says big AI growth fueled revenue jump
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: SpaceX reported a massive 161% year-over-year revenue jump in Q3, reaching $14.6 billion.
The growth was explicitly attributed to the 'Super Intelligence (SI) segment' and accelerated Connectivity services.
While the Space division incurred a $7 million operational loss, the Connectivity group was profitable, posting $2.4 million in operations.

stories.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is modifying its commercial Terms of Service (TOS) regarding AI scraping following public backlash.
The change involves dropping the word 'train' from the policy, signaling a shift in how AI data usage is framed.
Crucially, Meta is reportedly not implementing language that respects robots.txt directives in its updated policy.

stories.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Discovery of 8 compromised TLS certificates poses a significant security risk to the internet.
The vulnerability lies in intermediate certificates, which allow unauthorized parties to mint web credentials for any server.
This incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in current internet security infrastructure.

stories.title: ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
stories.author: Fenglei Fan
bullet_points: Introduces ACE-Compression, a new evaluation framework for compressed Large Language Models (LLMs).
Argues that standard task performance metrics are insufficient for assessing the impact of model compression.
Focuses on identifying which underlying 'abilities' survive or collapse during the compression process, rather than just final task scores.

stories.title: Polarity Blindness in LLM Safety: A Systematic Study of Negation, Antonym Substitution, and Adversarial Framing
stories.author: Nuria Oliver
bullet_points: Identifies 'polarity blindness' as a critical vulnerability in LLM safety guardrails.
Demonstrates that LLMs fail to recognize harmful intent after linguistic transformations like negation and antonym substitution.
The research systematically studies how polarity-altering language can bypass existing safety mechanisms.

stories.title: CollabSciReM: Aligning Language Models for Scientific Conversations via Science-Aware Reward Decomposition
stories.author: Sören Auer
bullet_points: Introduces CollabSciReM, a method to align LLMs specifically for scientific conversations.
Addresses the limitations of current LLM alignment, which often sacrifice accuracy or efficiency for conversational fluency.
Aims to create scientifically rigorous assistants that are accurate, logically consistent, and token-efficient for research collaboration.

stories.title: From Tokens to Files: Multi-Granularity Detection and Localization of AI-Involved Code
stories.author: Bolei He
bullet_points: Addresses the growing need to distinguish human-written code from code generated or modified by Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes a method for multi-granularity detection, moving beyond simple file-level scoring to localize AI-contributed lines or blocks.
Targets the limitation of existing methods, which average out evidence when AI involvement is localized to small portions of a file.

stories.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
stories.author: Sangdoo Yun
bullet_points: Introduces LaLa-World, a Language-conditioned Latent World Model (LWM).
Demonstrates that JEPA-style LWMs can learn across diverse domains by integrating natural language actions.
Establishes the model as an efficient foundation for planning via imagination and subsequent policy fine-tuning.

stories.title: Polarity Blindness in LLM Safety: A Systematic Study of Negation, Antonym Substitution, and Adversarial Framing
stories.author: Nuria Oliver
bullet_points: Identifies 'polarity blindness' as a critical vulnerability in LLM safety guardrails.
Demonstrates how linguistic transformations (negation and antonym substitution) can bypass safety filters.
Systematically studies the failure of LLMs to recognize harmful intent after polarity-altering language.

stories.title: From Tokens to Files: Multi-Granularity Detection and Localization of AI-Involved Code
stories.author: Bolei He
bullet_points: Addresses the growing problem of distinguishing human-written code from code generated or modified by Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes a method for multi-granularity detection, moving beyond single-file scoring to localize AI contributions at the line or block level.
Highlights a critical need in the AI development lifecycle for provenance tracking and accountability in AI-assisted software engineering.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users can access and run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks like software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is offered for free access through Ollama Cloud for a limited promotional period.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure and accessible deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for answering questions.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring based on text input.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: YouTube is reportedly testing a change to hide the dislike button on videos.
Evidence of this change includes users reporting the button moved to the three-dots submenu or being absent entirely.
This shift represents a potential change in user feedback mechanisms on the platform.

stories.title: Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Oura is enhancing its smart ring capabilities with new cardiovascular health tracking features.
The updates include 'Cardio Effort' and automatic VO2 Max tracking.
The goal is to help users optimize their exercise routines for long-term health.

stories.title: Quantum-JEPA: Quantum Born Priors for Latent-Action JEPA World Models
stories.author: Haiyu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces Quantum-JEPA, a novel framework combining quantum generative models with JEPA for world modeling.
Addresses the inherent uncertainty in world modeling by learning distributions of future representations.
Utilizes a conditional quantum Born prior and circuit measurements to generate binary latent actions for prediction.

stories.title: MMEnterprise-Bench: Evaluating Enterprise Agents over Evolving Multimodal Records
stories.author: Hyunwoo J. Kim
bullet_points: Introduces MMEnterprise-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating enterprise AI agents.
Focuses on agents' ability to answer questions over dynamic, evolving workplace records (documents, chats, figures).
Highlights the critical need for agents to handle temporal conflicts, cross-source inconsistencies, and evidence insufficiency.

stories.title: The Shape of the DPO Hyperparameter Landscape: What to Measure, How It Moves with Scale, and When Not to Transfer It
stories.author: Aaron Klein
bullet_points: The paper investigates the hyperparameter sensitivity of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), a key technique in language model fine-tuning.
It analyzes how optimal DPO hyperparameters (like learning rate and $\beta$) change as the underlying model scale increases.
The research provides guidance on the limitations of transferring hyperparameters across different model sizes.

stories.title: Near-Duplicate Image Selection Transfers Preferences in Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Seunghyun Kim
bullet_points: Investigates 'subliminal learning,' where model preferences transfer without explicit data cues.
Examines if selecting near-duplicate images during data curation can transfer preferences in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
The study tests this by having curators select one of eight near-duplicate variants based on caption likelihood.

stories.title: The Shape of the DPO Hyperparameter Landscape: What to Measure, How It Moves with Scale, and When Not to Transfer It
stories.author: Aaron Klein
bullet_points: The paper investigates the hyperparameter sensitivity of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), a key technique in language model fine-tuning.
It systematically analyzes how optimal DPO hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate, $\beta$) change as the underlying model scale increases.
The research aims to provide guidance on when and how to transfer hyperparameter settings across different model sizes.

stories.title: Elicitation or Expansion? Demystifying Gains from Agent Harness Optimization
stories.author: Wonjun Kang
bullet_points: Harness optimization in language model agents can yield significant performance gains without requiring model weight updates.
A well-designed harness improves agent capability by effectively managing context, tool usage, and execution workflows.
The research distinguishes between 'elicitation' (better performance on known tasks) and 'expansion' (solving a wider range of tasks) due to harness optimization.

stories.title: SAPD: Learning from Agent Experience without Environment Interaction
stories.author: Xunliang Cai
bullet_points: The research addresses a key bottleneck in scaling LLM agents: the need for extensive, costly environment interaction during training.
The proposed method, SAPD, aims to leverage existing offline trajectory data to refine agent policies without requiring continuous environment interaction.
It seeks to overcome limitations of current offline RL techniques, such as catastrophic forgetting associated with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT).

stories.title: From Generic to Dedicated: A Novel Optimizer for Online Continual Learning
stories.author: Sen Lin
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in Online Continual Learning (OCL) models.
It proposes a novel optimizer specifically designed for OCL, moving beyond generic optimizers like SGD and AdamW.
The core contribution involves linking optimization dynamics to OCL requirements by recasting Polyak-Ruppert averaging.

stories.title: ProVe: Proposer-Verifier Decoding
stories.author: Aixin Sun
bullet_points: ProVe introduces a novel decoding technique that reverses the roles in speculative decoding.
A large model is fine-tuned as a 'proposer' to predict blocks of tokens in one pass, which are then verified.
This method aims to accelerate autoregressive language models by leveraging parallel verification.

stories.title: ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
stories.author: Fenglei Fan
bullet_points: The paper introduces ACE-Compression, a new evaluation framework for compressed Large Language Models (LLMs).
It argues that standard performance metrics are insufficient because compression perturbs underlying distributed knowledge.
ACE-Compression aims to reveal which specific 'abilities' survive or collapse during the model compression process.

stories.title: CollabSciReM: Aligning Language Models for Scientific Conversations via Science-Aware Reward Decomposition
stories.author: Sören Auer
bullet_points: The paper introduces CollabSciReM, a method to align LLMs specifically for scientific conversations.
The goal is to create research collaborators that are accurate, methodologically justified, and logically consistent, addressing limitations in current alignment techniques.
The research tackles the trade-off where general instruction-tuned models often sacrifice scientific rigor for conversational verbosity.

stories.title: Testing Associative Creativity in Humans and Multimodal LLMs with Difficult-to-Name Visual Stimuli
stories.author: Sina Zarrieß
bullet_points: The research investigates associative creativity by comparing human performance against multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
It specifically tests how humans and models handle abstract visual stimuli that are difficult to map onto known semantic concepts.
Creativity is evaluated across two dimensions: originality and effectiveness, using state-of-the-art MLLMs.

stories.title: SciDiagBench: A Type-Specific Benchmark for Human-Aligned Evaluation of Scientific Diagrams
stories.author: Tian Tian
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagBench, a new benchmark for evaluating scientific diagram generation.
Addresses the limitation of existing VLM benchmarks by focusing on type-specific evaluation criteria.
Aims to align AI evaluation with how human experts assess the quality of diverse scientific diagrams.

stories.title: SlopCodeBench 10/2026 – Opus 5.5, Astra wins overall, xhigh considered harmful
stories.author: dhorthy
bullet_points: SlopCodeBench is a novel benchmark designed to test AI models by progressively revealing features (checkpoints) within a single, continuous codebase challenge.
This methodology aims to better simulate real-world software development workflows compared to traditional, isolated task benchmarks.
The latest results (10/2026) show Opus 5.5 and Astra performing well, while 'xhigh' was flagged as potentially harmful.

stories.title: Your agent's retry bug isn't an AI problem. It's a distributed-systems problem with an LLM on top.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: The article argues that common failures in AI agents (like retry bugs) stem from underlying distributed systems issues, not the LLM itself.
It critiques the typical 'happy path' demonstration of AI agents, which overlooks real-world complexity.
The piece suggests that robust agent development requires addressing distributed systems challenges layered beneath the LLM interface.

stories.title: Stress-Testing Gemini 4 Argon: Building a 3D Flutter Kart Game in 15 Prompts with Zero Assets
stories.author: leehack
bullet_points: The article explores using frontier models (like Gemini 4 Argon) for complex, creative coding tasks.
It demonstrates building a 3D Flutter game using only 15 prompts and zero pre-existing assets.
The piece highlights a gap in current AI coding benchmarks, which often focus only on standard web apps or CRUD interfaces.
